ownership: Muse provides this contract and its test cases only. Scorer code is implemented by the main developer; this file is not code and must not be executed as a scorer.

source_runtime.runtime_branch_head_subject: qa(core20k): establish fail-closed dual AI review pilot for 30 matched KUs
source_runtime.retrieval_method: git fetch from origin (https) + git show to local files; gzip decompressed locally. No GitHub push, no main modification, no Runtime/SRS/learning-record write.

normalisation: Curly apostrophe U+2019 -> straight apostrophe U+0027 (equivalent). A straight-vs-curly difference alone must NEVER fail an answer.
Casefold (case-insensitive comparison). Sentence-initial capitalisation (e.g. Remote) therefore passes, and capitalised inflections pass.
After normalisation, require exact equality with the canonical answer. No stemming, no lemma fallback, no edit-distance tolerance.
Answers must be a single token (no spaces). Multi-token input is rejected even if it contains the canonical form.
mandatory_suffix_rule: For the five contracted items, the inflected or possessive suffix is part of the answer. The bare lemma is REJECTED even though it is a real word: function != functions, strike != struck, degree != degrees, master != master's, academic != academics. This is the direct lesson of the B188 extra error: surface form, not lemma identity, is what the item teaches.

items.example_en: The old machine still functions well.
An idea suddenly struck me on the bus.
items.prompt: An idea suddenly ___ me on the bus.
items.why_inflected: Past-tense narrative requires the irregular past form, not the base form or regularised *striked.

items.example_en: The temperature rose by three degrees.
She earned a master's degree in chemistry.
items.prompt: She earned a ___ degree in chemistry.
items.why_inflected: The degree name is master's degree; master's is a genitive noun, not an adjective, and the apostrophe+s is mandatory. 'master' alone must fail, while master's with either apostrophe shape must pass.

items.example_en: The conference attracted academics from many countries.
items.prompt: The conference attracted ___ from many countries.
items.why_inflected: Plural context ('from many countries', attracted people) requires the plural noun.

items.example_en: Remote access lets staff work from home.
items.prompt: ___ access lets staff work from home.
items.why_inflected: Sentence-initial capitalisation only: 'remote' (lowercase) must also pass after casefold normalisation; this is a case policy, not an inflection rule, and must not be confused with the suffix rule above.

fail_closed: If the scorer cannot normalise an input (undecodable bytes, empty input), it must REJECT, not guess. If Runtime SHA, ku_id, kind, or gloss changes, the contracted items must be re-verified before scoring resumes.
